**A book is not stored as one removable file inside the weights.** The same parameters help represent grammar, common facts, and many overlapping passages. Gradient ascent on the book's token loss makes those sequences less likely, but it moves shared parameters that also support unrelated text. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.07406)

For example, suppressing a sentence containing a common scientific fact may reduce useful factual knowledge as well as memorized wording. Conversely, making one exact passage unlikely may leave a paraphrase or an alternative extraction prompt effective. The optimization target and the desired forgetting claim are different.

**Compare forgetting with retention.** Define what must be removed: verbatim reproduction, identifiable personal facts, membership evidence, or influence of particular training records. Then evaluate that target alongside general fluency and neighboring legitimate knowledge. A model refusing a familiar prompt shows a behavioral response; it does not establish that the information is absent from its parameters.

Retraining without the disputed data is a useful reference when feasible, though even that model may know overlapping information from other sources. Approximate unlearning combines targeted changes with constraints that preserve retained behavior, but strong claims require stated access and attack assumptions. Test paraphrases, alternate prompts, and extraction strategies on held-out cases. Gradient ascent is one possible update direction, not a certificate of complete removal.

**Technical details and references.**

Knowledge is distributed across shared parameters, so increasing loss on a forget set can damage neighboring useful capabilities and still fail to remove all recoverable information. Paraphrases, alternate prompts, and memorized fragments may survive. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.07406) [2](https://www.deeplearningbook.org/contents/regularization.html)

Evaluate unlearning against a retrained-without-data reference where feasible, using held-out related facts, extraction attempts, membership tests with known limitations, and retained-task utility. Combine targeted updates with retention objectives or localized mechanisms, but do not equate refusal at inference with deletion from weights.

Track training-data provenance and exact scope of the removal request. Gradient ascent is an optimization operation, not a certificate of legal or technical erasure. Strong claims require defined adversary/access assumptions and evidence beyond a small set of prompted examples.
